operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: as predictions_porous_plug.json's: D = 1, nu = rho = 1, g = 8, steady Stokes, the default band; a plug one diameter long closing the lumen in a period of four; D/h 16, 32, 64; the 0.1h and 0.01h interiors; sqrt(K)/h 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, 0.001; the CG's tolerance 1e-8 (the default) and 1e-10, its cap 250000
operating_point.seeds_and_draws: none drawn: each row one deterministic case

gate_1_floor_intercept.claim: the floor, the flux a closing plug lets past it whatever its permeability, is the intercept of Q / Q_open against K over the converged rows (Q = leak + C K)
gate_1_floor_intercept.case: probe/measure.py parallel arms, through the FVM node's own steady step

prediction.value: the intercept within its resolution of zero at every D/h and both interiors, so stated as a bound: |leak| / Q_open under about 1e-3 of the smallest converged row's flux, about 4e-9 / 1e-9 / 3e-10 at D/h 16 / 32 / 64 with sqrt(K)/h 0.003 converged; the two interiors the same within it
prediction.basis: derived: the parallel form gives every face in the plug's span, the wall's solid too, at least 1/K (100/K where the face holds no fluid), so no path around the plug escapes its resistance; the resolution from the drift of the series' error with sqrt(K)/h (about 0.1 % a factor of three, seen_before)
prediction.why: a constant leak needs a path that does not carry the plug's resistivity; the parallel form's reach leaves none

gate_1_floor_intercept.metric: the intercept over Q_open, and its resolution: the spread of the pairwise intercepts of the converged rows, and the change of each row's Q between the tolerances 1e-8 and 1e-10

control.plant: the share form (the plug's depth not carried into the wall's solid), whose floor is a real constant leak through the wall's stiff interior around the plug
control.expected_rate: 1/1 per arm (deterministic): the intercept from its converged rows equals its sqrt(K)/h 1e-3 row within 3 %, and is many times the parallel form's bound
control.resolution: the parallel form's bound: a leak above it is seen

gate_1_floor_intercept.if_wrong: a non-zero intercept above the resolution is a path around the plug; the build report then states the measured floor and the validity line its ratio, as the brief asks
gate_1_floor_intercept.cannot_discriminate_if: fewer than two rows converge at a D/h and interior, or the pairwise intercepts disagree by more than they differ from zero

gate_2_floor_convergence.claim: which small permeabilities the CG reaches

prediction.value: sqrt(K)/h 0.003 converges at every D/h, about three times the iterations at 0.01 (about 9000 / 20000 / 45000 at D/h 16 / 32 / 64); 0.001 stops stagnated, flagged, as the floor arms did; 1e-10 converges at 0.03 and 0.01, about 25 % more iterations than 1e-8
prediction.basis: measured-before (seen_before: the iterations rose about 2.8 times from 0.03 to 0.01; the floor arms at 1e-3 stagnated); a guess for 1e-10
prediction.why: the penalty's contrast with the fluid's operator, h^2 / K, grows tenfold a factor of three in sqrt(K)/h, and Jacobi does not remove its coupling through the projection

gate_3_floor_tolerance.claim: the rows' fluxes are converged well below the intercept's resolution

prediction.value: each row's Q at 1e-10 within 1e-4 of its value at 1e-8 (relative), wherever both converge
prediction.why: the CG's true residual at 1e-8 relative to the drive; the plug's flux is small but the penalty carries the drive, so the residual measures the Darcy balance itself
